[THOUGHT]  
This is a classic presentation of acute lumbar radiculopathy due to a focal disc herniation at L5–S1. The patient is young, healthy, with no systemic symptoms (no fever, weight loss, night pain), and no red flags (no bowel/bladder dysfunction, no saddle anesthesia, no motor weakness, no reflex asymmetry). The radicular pain follows the L5–S1 distribution — lateral leg to foot — consistent with S1 nerve root involvement (though note: L5 radiculopathy typically radiates to lateral thigh/leg and dorsum of foot; S1 more commonly involves posterior calf and lateral/sole of foot; however, the MRI confirms L5–S1 disc herniation *with nerve root impingement*, and clinical correlation favors S1 given radiation to foot and positive SLR — which is most sensitive for S1). Crucially, all neurologic exam findings are *intact*: strength (dorsiflexion = L4/L5, great toe extension = L5, plantarflexion = S1), sensation (L5 dermatome tested and intact), and reflexes (Achilles = S1, patellar = L3/L4) are normal — confirming *no motor deficit or sensory loss*, i.e., a pure *pain-dominant* radiculopathy without neurologic compromise. The MRI definitively shows disc herniation at L5–S1 with nerve root impingement and excludes emergent mimics (e.g., cauda equina syndrome, tumor, infection, fracture). The absence of central stenosis or cord compression further supports a focal, mechanical, self-limited process. Conservative management is appropriate and prognosis excellent.

- Acute onset of sharp, radicular low back pain during physical activity (mechanical trigger)  
- Pain radiates along the lateral leg to the foot (S1 or L5 dermatomal pattern)

- Positive straight-leg raise test (9/10 — highly sensitive for S1 radiculopathy)  
- Intact strength in dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, and great toe extension (no motor deficit)  
- Intact light touch and pinprick sensation over L5 dermatome (no sensory deficit)  
- Normal patellar and Achilles reflexes (no reflex abnormality)  
- Lumbar MRI confirms L5–S1 disc herniation with nerve root impingement  
- No bowel/bladder dysfunction, fever, weight loss, or neurologic deficits (absence of red flags)  
- No central canal stenosis, cauda equina compression, or other pathology on MRI  

[GAPS]  
- MRI does not specify whether the herniation is paracentral, foraminal, or extraforaminal — but this does not alter the primary diagnosis  
- No EMG/NCS performed — but not indicated acutely in absence of motor/sensory deficits  
- No documentation of Valsalva or cough exacerbation — but not required for diagnosis  
- None  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Acute S1 radiculopathy secondary to L5–S1 disc herniation
